title: Today Stays Today
lede: If the app stayed open past midnight, the Schedule labelled today's events as "Tomorrow". Day labels now update when the date changes.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.note: There's no matched before/after pair. The bug only shows when the app stays open past midnight, and a simulator capture can't reproduce that. The reported screenshot is the user's own device; the after capture is a fixture run on GT Capture iPhone 18 Pro Max, light mode, at the top of the list.

changes.was: The day headers checked the clock only when they first drew. Nothing redrew them at midnight, so an app left open overnight kept Thursday's labels on Friday.
changes.now: A shared today value, set where the app starts, updates at midnight, on clock or time-zone changes, and when the app returns to the foreground. Headers, rows, the week strip and the list's first day all use it.

changes.h: Day 2 of a multi-day event read "Now" a day early
changes.was: Saturday's "Day 2 of 2" row showed Now on Friday.
changes.now: Each day of a multi-day event shows Now only on its own day.

changes.was: Event detail, Published Schedule, Home due-today colors, Profile Next Up, notification groups, booking day labels and kiosk sections each checked the clock directly.
changes.now: They all use the shared today value. A guard test fails if any iOS code checks today, tomorrow or yesterday against the clock directly.

verification: CurrentDayTests: 2 tests pass, including the midnight boundary
vitest: 712 test files pass, 1 skipped (includes the new guard test)
ScheduleScreenshotUITests/testScheduleListCaptures passed on GT Capture iPhone 18 Pro Max
notes: The fixture capture shows how the screen looks with the change. It can't show the screen changing at midnight; the unit tests and guard test cover that.
Web schedule views also read the current date when they draw, so a browser tab left open overnight can still go stale. That isn't covered here.
